4.text: high look--(Compare Margin; Psa 131:1). proud heart--or, "heart of breadth," one that is swollen (compare Psa 101:5). ploughing--better "lamp," a frequent figure for prosperity (Pro 20:20); hence joy or delight.

5.text: The contrast is between steady industry and rashness (compare Pro 19:2).

6.text: The getting--or, "what is obtained" (compare Job 7:2; Jer 22:13, Hebrew). vanity . . . to and fro--as fleeting as chaff or stubble in the wind (compare Pro 20:17-21; Psa 62:10). Such gettings are unsatisfactory. them . . . death--act as if they did (Pro 8:36; Pro 17:19).

7.text: robbery--or, "destruction," especially oppression, of which they are authors. shall destroy--literally, "cut with a saw" (Kg1 7:9), that is, utterly ruin them. Their sins shall be visited on them in kind. to do judgment--what is just and right.

8.text: of man--any one; his way is opposed to truth, and also estranged from it. The pure proves himself such by his right conduct.

9.text: corner--a turret or arbor on the roof. brawling--or contentious. wide house--literally, "house of fellowship," large enough for several families.

10.text: So strongly does he desire to do evil (Psa 10:3; Ecc 8:11), that he will not even spare his friend if in his way.

11.text: (Compare Pro 19:25). That which the simple learn by the terrors of punishment, the wise learn by teaching.

12.text: (Compare Psa 37:35-38; Psa 73:17, Psa 73:20). house--family or interests. overthroweth--either supply "God" (compare Pro 10:24), or the word is used impersonally.

13.text: The principles of retribution, often taught (compare Psa 18:26; Mat 7:1-12).

14.text: The effect of bribery (Pro 17:23) is enhanced by secrecy, as the bribed person does not wish his motives made known.

15.text: But the just love right and need no bribes. The wicked at last meet destruction, though for a time happy in concealing corruption.

16.text: the way of understanding--(Compare Pro 12:26; Pro 14:22). remain--that is, rest as at a journey's end; death will be his unchanging home.

18.text: (Compare Pro 11:8). By suffering what they had devised for the righteous, or brought on them, the wicked became their ransom, in the usual sense of substitutes (compare Jos 7:26; Est 7:9).

20.text: The wise, by diligence and care, lay up and increase wealth, while fools spend--literally, "swallow it up," greedily.

21.text: He who tries to act justly and kindly (Psa 34:14) will prosper and obtain justice and honor.

22.text: "Wisdom is better than strength" (Ecc 7:19; Ecc 9:15). strength . . . thereof--that in which they confide.

24.text: The reproachful name is deserved by those who treat others with anger and contempt.

25.text: desire--that is, of ease and idleness brings him to starvation.

26.text: The sin of covetousness marks the sluggard, as the virtue of benevolence the righteous.

27.text: God regards the heart, and hypocrisy is more odious than open inconsistency. wicked mind--or, "design" (Pro 1:4).

28.text: (Compare Pro 19:5). that heareth--or heeds instruction, and so grows wise. speaketh constantly--or sincerely (compare Hab 1:5), and hence is believed (Pro 12:19; Jam 1:19).

29.text: hardeneth his face--is obstinate. directeth . . . way--considers it, and acts advisedly.

30.text: Men's best devices and reliances are vain compared with God's, or without His aid (Pro 19:21; Psa 20:7; Psa 33:17). Next: Proverbs Chapter 22
